answer: Graph-based trust routing secures a peer meadow by tracing random walks from verified anchors toward a consensus summit. An attacker attempting a Sybil attack incurs the scarce cost of cultivating authentic, reciprocal trust edges with honest nodes to cross topological bottlenecks. Verification proofs are recorded on an immutable marble ledger. However, this architecture inherently marginalizes benign newcomer agents that lack prior interaction history.
